contract.notes: Provider-neutral upstream IdP adapter. Autheory is the first and only adapter in this program. The SPI is deliberately the minimum needed to derive the facade from requirements; provider-specific policy travels through hints and errors, never through framework branches.

operations.name: Discovery
operations.purpose: OIDC/RFC 8414 discovery bootstrap; verify issuer equality before trusting any endpoint.

operations.name: AuthorizationURL
operations.purpose: Build the upstream authorize URL the browser is redirected to from /authorize.

operations.name: ExchangeCode
operations.purpose: Server-side upstream code exchange presenting the facade's own client and PKCE verifier.
fail_closed: error body is never forwarded to the client

operations.name: Refresh
operations.purpose: Upstream refresh presenting the OAuth client that owns the recorded upstream material.
fail_closed: secret-bearing error body is never forwarded

operations.name: ValidateAccessToken
operations.purpose: Fail-closed validation before broker mutation or client response; never mutates the token.

notes.state: fresh upstream state, distinct from the client's state
notes.hints: opaque provider hints (e.g. account_id); the provider derives authentication account context from its own validated binding, never from the hint

notes.upstream_client_id: the client that owns the recorded upstream material; the facade client store is the discriminator

TokenSet.notes: id_token, when present, is dropped by the facade and never returned to the client

autheory_adapter.discovery: RFC 8414 / OIDC configuration; authorization_endpoint published as issuer + /oauth/authorize; jwks_uri = /.well-known/jwks.json; registration_endpoint = /register
autheory_adapter.refresh_binding: refresh material is bound to the OAuth client it was issued to

legacy_client_verify.purpose: backs optional app-side legacy client adoption (policy, not framework)

autheory_adapter.account_hint: account_id hint semantics are an Autheory contract detail; passed through as an opaque hint

invariants: The upstream is the sole token minting authority; the facade never signs or re-signs access tokens.
The upstream access token is returned to the client byte-for-byte unmodified.
Upstream authorization codes, refresh tokens, and id_token never reach the client.
Upstream error bodies are never forwarded verbatim to the client.
